title: Improving Temporal Relation Extraction with a Globally Acquired Statistical Resource
research_question: Can large-scale corpus-derived prior knowledge about the temporal ordering of event types improve local and globally constrained temporal-relation extraction?
methodology: The authors build TemProb by extracting verb-frame events and temporal relations from more than one million New York Times articles spanning 1987–2007, using semantic role labeling, learned temporal classifiers, and greedy transitive-closure inference. The resulting counts define prior distributions over temporal relations between pairs of semantic verb frames. They validate these priors against TimeBank-Dense and an EventCausality dataset, then inject the priors as features into local averaged-perceptron classifiers and as regularization terms in an ILP global inference model. Performance is evaluated using precision, recall, F1, temporal-awareness F-score, significance tests, and additional bootstrap stability analysis.

key_findings.finding: TemProb contains approximately 51,000 distinct verb semantic frames, 9.2 million verb-pair-relation entries, and up to about 80 million extracted temporal relations from the NYT corpus.
TemProb's before/after probabilities behave as meaningful confidence estimates on TimeBank-Dense: increasing the probability threshold raises precision while reducing recall.
On the converted EventCausality evaluation, using TemProb priors achieved 66.2% accuracy, an 11.5-point improvement over the majority T-Before baseline.

Adding the full TemProb prior distribution as local classifier features improved F1 by 2.7 points for same-sentence relations and 6.5 points for adjacent-sentence relations relative to the original local features.

Combining TemProb features and ILP regularization increased global TimeBank-Dense F1 from 46.2 to 52.1 and temporal-awareness F-score from 42.5 to 49.6, with the reported comparison significant at p<0.0005.
On the paper's partial TimeBank-Dense evaluation restricted to SRL-extracted verb events, the proposed system achieved F1=55.5 and temporal-awareness F=52.8, exceeding the two compared prior systems.
The resource is restricted to verb semantic-frame events and therefore does not directly cover nominal events or all events in complete TimeBank-Dense.
The automatically induced resource contains erroneous or context-sensitive event-pair statistics, particularly because event arguments and richer context are not represented in the pairwise priors.

limitations: TemProb is derived from New York Times news, so its event-order priors may be domain-specific and may not transfer directly to workplace email, chat, or operational logs.
Only verb semantic frames are modeled; nominal and other event types are omitted.
The event-pair statistics ignore arguments, which can make apparently anomalous temporal associations difficult to distinguish from extraction errors or special contexts.
TemProb is automatically generated using an imperfect temporal-relation extraction system, so extraction errors are propagated into the resource.
The training annotations and generated relations primarily cover same-sentence or adjacent-sentence event pairs, limiting direct modeling of longer-range relations.
The main comparison focuses on a partial TimeBank-Dense subset that matches SRL-extracted verb events rather than the complete benchmark.
The global regularization weight was heuristically fixed at 0.5 rather than selected through a reported systematic optimization.
Evaluation of EventCausality as temporal data assumes that causes temporally precede their effects.
The resource models typical temporal order, not event factuality, cancellation, revision, source authority, or contradiction states.
raw_claims: Temporal-relation decisions often require knowledge about the order in which event types usually occur.
TemProb was induced automatically from more than one million New York Times documents covering roughly twenty years.
Events are represented as disambiguated verb semantic frames extracted with semantic role labeling.
The temporal label set contains before, after, includes, included, equal, and vague.
Two temporal classifiers are trained separately for same-sentence and neighboring-sentence event pairs.
Greedy graph inference applies transitive closure whenever a new temporal relation is added.
The induced resource contains around 51,000 unique verb frames and roughly 80 million extracted relations.
Some verb pairs have highly stable tendencies to occur in one temporal order across the corpus.
Higher TemProb before-or-after confidence thresholds yield higher precision on TimeBank-Dense at the cost of recall.
The TemProb prior improved accuracy over a majority-label baseline on the EventCausality-derived temporal task.
Prior-distribution features produced larger gains for adjacent-sentence pairs than for same-sentence pairs.
Adding TemProb priors to both local classification and global ILP inference improved F1 and temporal-awareness scores.
The global model enforces uniqueness, symmetry, and transitivity constraints while rewarding agreement with TemProb.
TemProb does not cover all TimeBank-Dense events because it is restricted to events identified through verb SRL.
The authors made both the reported system and the TemProb resource publicly available.
